"1. Classic Wii Sports Overview @COMMENT_BODY@ Character Creator
​The Mii Character Creator @COMMENT_BODY@ Customization: In the original Wii Sports, players used the Mii Channel to build custom avatars. Customization included selecting gender, height, and build (skinny to wide), along with specific facial geometry: head shapes, hairstyles, eyebrows, eyes, noses, mouths, facial hair, glasses, and favorite colors (which dictated outfit colors).  
​The Nostalgic Body @COMMENT_BODY@ Anatomy: Characters feature the iconic Wii Sports proportions—floating spherical hands with no arms, capsule-shaped torsos, stubby legs/feet, and simple, expressive faces.
​The Five Core Sports:  
​1. Tennis: Doubles matches where footwork is automated, focusing on swing timing, angle, and spin (topspin/backspin).  
​2. Baseball: 3-inning games where you bat (timing swings for hits/home runs) and pitch (throwing fastballs, curveballs, screwballs, and splitters).
​3. Golf: 3-hole or 9-hole courses (Beginner, Intermediate, Expert) where players account for wind speed, elevation, and green slope.  
​4. Boxing: 3-round matches where you guard your face/body, dodge left/right, and throw jabs, hooks, and uppercuts to knock down your opponent.  
​5. Bowling: Standard 10-frame bowling where you adjust position, angle, and wrist twist to hook the ball into the pocket for strikes and spares.  
​2. Custom Game Concept / Prompt Specification
​If you are looking to pitch, build, or generate a modern remake or Roblox/web-game version of Wii Sports with your exact specifications, here is the complete feature list structured as a clear specification:
​Visuals @COMMENT_BODY@ Nostalgic Environment
​100% Nostalgic Aesthetics: Every map must retain the exact, iconic low-poly nostalgic aesthetic of the original Wii Sports—including the classic grass textures and models, the distinct chunky/layered nostalgic trees, the classic blue skybox with soft white clouds, and the nostalgic water shaders/physics around the golf courses and stadiums.
​Classic Character Models: Include a full built-in Mii-style character creator featuring the exact nostalgic body proportions, floating sphere hands, stubby legs, classic facial features (eyes, mouths, noses, eyebrows), and original hairstyles from Wii Sports.
​Upgraded Realism, Physics @COMMENT_BODY@ Swipe Controls
​Enhanced Physics Engine: Upgrade the ball aerodynamics, grass friction, pin collisions, water splashes, and impact physics for realistic bounce, spin, and momentum while keeping the nostalgic visual look.
​Touch / Mouse Swipe Mechanics:
​Tennis @COMMENT_BODY@ Baseball: Swipe up/forward to swing the racket or bat, or swipe up to pitch/throw the ball, with swipe speed and angle determining power and curve.
​Bowling: Swipe up to roll the ball down the lane, curving your swipe to add spin.
​Golf: Select your specific golf club type (Driver, Wood, Iron, Wedge, Putter) based on distance and terrain, aim your shot, and swipe up to whack the golf ball with realistic loft and backspin.
​Boxing: Swipe up/forward to throw punches and swipe side-to-side to dodge.
​Game Modes @COMMENT_BODY@ Online Matchmaking
​Flexible Match Formats: Every sport supports 1v1 and 2v2 modes.
​AI or Online Multiplayer: Players can choose to play solo/co-op against CPU AI (featuring classic tiered difficulty opponents) or real players online.
​Matchmaking UI @COMMENT_BODY@ Timer: Selecting Online mode triggers a clean, nostalgic UI screen displaying \"Loading... Matchmaking\" alongside a live elapsed timer showing exactly how long you have been searching for a match.
​Full Interactive Audio @COMMENT_BODY@ Sound Effects
​Complete UI @COMMENT_BODY@ Gameplay SFX: Every single interactive element must have crisp, nostalgic sound effects—including menu button clicks, hover chimes, matchmaking search pulses and match-found fanfares, racket/bat hits, golf club swings and ball-in-cup rattles, bowling pin crashes, boxing glove thuds, and crowd cheers.Interactive Action @COMMENT_BODY@ Shot-Style HUD Buttons
​During gameplay, players have a clean, responsive HUD featuring sleek, glowing, tactile buttons on the screen. Every button press triggers a distinct, satisfying interactive click/lock-in sound effect and visual highlight to confirm your selected technique before or during your swipe.
​1. Boxing Controls
​Left Hook: Curls a heavy horizontal punch toward the opponent's right side (triggers a sharp whoosh-snap UI lock-in sound).
​Right Hook: Delivers a power hook toward the opponent's left side.
​Uppercut: Launches a rising close-range strike to break through high guards (triggers a heavy bass chime).
​Straight Strike / Jab: Fast, direct punch to interrupt opponent combos.
​High / Low Block: Raises both floating sphere gloves to absorb incoming punches with a muffled leather thud.
​Left @COMMENT_BODY@ Right Dodge: Quick-step weaves to evade hooks and straight punches, opening up counter-attack windows.
​2. Tennis Shot-Style Buttons
​Topspin: Dips the ball rapidly over the net with high forward bounce after landing (high-pitched zip button sound).
​Backspin / Slice: Keeps the ball low and skidding across the nostalgic grass court.
​Lob: Lofts the ball high into the nostalgic blue sky over an opponent rushing the net.
​Flat Power Shot: High-velocity line drive with minimal spin for finishing points.
​3. Baseball Pitching @COMMENT_BODY@ Batting Buttons
​When Pitching:
​Fastball: Maximum velocity straight down the plate (sharp pop SFX).
​Curveball: Wide sweeping horizontal/diagonal break across the strike zone.
​Screwball: Breaks sharply in the opposite direction of a curveball.
​Splitter: Drops suddenly right before reaching home plate.
​When Batting:
​Power Swing: Full-force swing aimed at hitting home runs out of the stadium.
​Contact Swing: Controlled, wide-zone swing for reliable base hits.
​Bunt: Softly taps the ball into the infield grass to advance runners.
​4. Golf Club @COMMENT_BODY@ Shot-Shaping Buttons
​Club Selector Buttons: Quick-tap buttons to cycle between Driver, Wood, Iron, Wedge, and Putter (accompanied by a metallic club-clink SFX).
​Full Swing / Approach / Chip: Adjusts backswing power cap for long fairways versus delicate green-side shots.
​Backspin Toggle: Adds heavy reverse spin so the ball bites and stops dead on the green.
​5. Bowling Spin @COMMENT_BODY@ Release Buttons
​Straight Ball: Locks the ball path for clean spare pickups.
​Left Hook / Right Hook: Pre-sets curve bias before you swipe up to roll the ball into the 1-3 or 1-2 pocket (triggers a subtle click-whir sound).
​Power Throw / Loft Toggle: Adjusts release speed and early-lane bounce.​Starting Title Screen @COMMENT_BODY@ Main Lobby Addition
​Title Screen: Opens on a bright, panoramic flyover of the nostalgic Wii Sports island—showcasing the classic blue sky, white clouds, nostalgic trees, and sparkling water—with the iconic Wii Sports logo centered on screen and a pulsing \"Press to Start\" prompt while the classic Wii Sports theme music plays in the background.
​Interactive Start Transition: Pressing or clicking \"Press to Start\" triggers the signature upbeat Wii Sports confirmation chime and smoothly transitions into the clean, white-and-blue glossy main menu lobby where players can enter the Character Creator or select any of the five sports.
​Complete Master Game Prompt (Ready to Copy @COMMENT_BODY@ Paste)
​Build a 3D Wii Sports remake featuring all five classic sports (Tennis, Baseball, Golf, Boxing, and Bowling) with upgraded realistic physics, touch/mouse swipe mechanics, online matchmaking, and 100% authentic Wii Sports visual and audio nostalgia.

​Boxing: Red or blue padded boxing gloves on both floating hands, plus protective headgear.

​Behind-the-Character Camera Perspective: Position the camera directly behind the player's character in every sport just like the original Wii Sports—over-the-shoulder/behind-the-back on the tennis court, behind the batter/pitcher at home plate and the mound, behind the golfer lining up their shot, translucent/over-the-shoulder behind the boxer in the ring, and directly behind the bowler facing down the lane.
​3. 100% Accurate Nostalgic Maps @COMMENT_BODY@ Upgraded Realism/Physics:
​Recreate every map with 100% fidelity to the original Wii Sports arenas, courses, and lanes—including the exact nostalgic grass models and textures, chunky layered trees, classic blue sky with soft white clouds, crowd Miis in the stands, and nostalgic water shaders/physics.

​Boxing: Left Hook, Right Hook, Uppercut, Straight Strike/Jab, High/Low Block, Left Dodge, Right Dodge.
​Tennis: Topspin, Backspin/Slice, Lob, Flat Power Shot.
​Baseball: Pitching (Fastball, Curveball, Screwball, Splitter) and Batting (Power Swing, Contact Swing, Bunt).
​Golf: Club Selector (Driver, Wood, Iron, Wedge, Putter), Shot Type (Full Swing, Approach, Chip), and Backspin Toggle.
​Bowling: Straight Ball, Left Hook, Right Hook, and Power/Loft Toggle.
​5. Game Modes, Online Matchmaking @COMMENT_BODY@ Full Sound Effects:
​Support 1v1 and 2v2 in every sport against either CPU AI (including classic Wii Sports champions like Matt) or real players online.
​Selecting Online mode displays a \"Loading... Matchmaking\" screen with a live elapsed timer counting how long you have been searching, accompanied by matchmaking search pulses and match-found fanfares.
​Include 100% authentic, crisp sound effects for every interactive element: menu button clicks, HUD shot-style selections, club clinks, racket/bat hits, pin crashes, boxing glove thuds, water splashes, announcer callouts (\"Strike!\", \"Home Run!\", \"Nice Shot!\"), and crowd cheers.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

- Build a complete, playable Wii Sports-inspired game in the existing project, with a title screen, lobby, character creator, and five sports.

## Requirements
- Include Tennis, Baseball, Golf, Boxing, and Bowling with sport-specific gameplay, controls, HUD actions, and scoring.
- Provide nostalgic low-poly-inspired visuals, Mii-style character customization, equipment, arenas, and audio.
- Support solo/co-op AI and online matchmaking, 1v1/2v2 formats, and an elapsed search timer.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; summarize assumptions when finished.
- Verify the game in a browser and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- The existing project is a plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript game; the updated screen design uses a canvas for the sport stage.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced `index.html` with title, lobby, character creator, matchmaking, and sports gameplay markup.
- Replaced `style.css` with responsive styling for the screens and game UI.
- Began replacing `script.js` with game state, sport configuration, scoring/action logic, audio, input listeners, and canvas drawing helpers.

### Active
- Finish and connect `script.js` to the markup; its current contents stop after `drawGolf`, and key functions/event wiring are still missing.
- Implement complete sport mechanics and character customization, navigation, sound toggle, and matchmaking cancellation.
- Run checks, verify gameplay in a browser, and capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `(none)`

1. Continue `script.js`: implement remaining sport renderers and `drawScene`, define `startLobby`, and wire screen navigation, character creator inputs, sport cards, exit, and sound controls.

3. Run available checks, capture and inspect a current JPEG, and report completed features and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Screen markup, IDs, buttons, and canvas.
- `style.css`: Screen styling, responsive layouts, and game UI.
- `script.js`: Current partial game logic and rendering; primary continuation point.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture helper.

- Changes are uncommitted; no checks or browser verification are recorded.
